A3_S6_D3: ^Calf: It’s you! These are the people who saved me, Mom!
^Anana: Thank you so much, you two. Did Chione pass on the jewelry as thanks?
^Noelle: Yes, it’s with me right now.
^Narrator: The monsteratops nods. From her kind tone, you can imagine that she smiled.
^Anana: These items are symbolic of our history on the island, and actions our ancestors took to protect this land.
^Anana: We have many stories of our own, which are told to the Viridi when they are young.
^Amelia: My ‘gran used to tell me that your kind were fierce warriors.
^Anana: Haha, perhaps back in the day — when predators and prey were still fighting over land.
^Anana: Our strength and size are gifts, so that we may protect what matters most.
^Anana: These days, such ‘protection’ is extended to the Viridi, along with any who identify themselves as Thavma.
^Noelle: I’ve noticed that the people here aren’t really concerned with species.
^Calf: It’s better that way, isn’t it?
^Calf: Birds can help us find items when they’re lost, while we can let them roost on our backs.
^Calf: …Last night, I was meaning to find something I buried nearby the ruins, to give to Oren. I thought it’d inspire a fun story.
^Calf: But everything looks the same at night… and I got stuck inside instead.
^Noelle: Some beetles noticed your trail in the ruins’ way, and a panther heard your cries.
^Amelia: “The forest remembers all who passed and still live within.”
^Anana: Maybe you should tell Oren about your adventure.
^Anana: He’s very good at spinning tales, after all.
